author: Codex paired difficulty assessor

source_artifacts.claim: The room defines the duct, low ferry, powered signal bridge, Isp-only ferry brake, two-weight DELIVERY pad, light sac, exits, and nearest-target boomerang.
Pads count accepted heroes and light crates as weight; active motor pads stop platforms and power pads enable required platforms.
A boomerang hit causes Isp dizzy or Pac shove with temporary effects and immunity.
Nearest-target boomerangs lock the nearer hero at windup, then launch after the authored cooldown/windup.
Boomerangs nudge light crates and can push Gem; this is the projectile's useful object interaction.
Dizzy reduces horizontal movement speed; shove adds temporary horizontal velocity.
Position 1, level_02, introduces Cana's boomerang attack; level_01 at lines 30-60 introduced a two-weight powered lift.
Position 8, level_08, introduces a movable light box that can hold a pad and coordinate with a partner.
Position 4, level_03, introduces using Isp on a hold pad to stop a moving ferry.

prior_knowledge.concept: Cana boomerang attacks and their temporary hero effects.

evidence.claim: Cana's boomerang is part of the first tutorial-room attack set; effects are defined by shared interference code.

prior_knowledge.concept: Two-weight power pads and riding a powered lift.

evidence.claim: Level_01 requires two weights to restore and power its lift, with a partner riding it.

prior_knowledge.concept: An Isp hold pad can brake a moving ferry.

evidence.claim: Level_03 gives Isp a hold STOP pad that disables a moving ferry motor.

prior_knowledge.concept: Light movable crates can hold pads and be repositioned with partner support.

evidence.claim: Level_08 includes a light movable box and an any-occupant hold pad.

mechanics.fact: Cana's boomerang selects the nearest hero at windup. In this room its 1.2-second windup and 1.2-second cooldown make its attacks repeatable. It can hit a hero, but it also nudges the room's light sac. Isp receives 0.6 seconds of dizzy movement at 55% speed; Pac receives a 0.4-second horizontal shove. These are temporary effects, not lethal hazards on this room's full-width gutter floor.

evidence.claim: Nearest-target boomerang configuration and its cooldown/windup.
The two hero-specific temporary effects and durations.
Projectile contact can push light crates.
The effects alter movement temporarily.

mechanics.fact: The light sac begins in the horizontal duct. The authored hint says to bait Cana's throw through the duct, move the sac onto the receiving ferry, and push it off while the ferry is low; a misplaced sac can be recovered from the gutter.

evidence.claim: Visible subtitle and authored hint describe nearest-hero aiming, sac nudging, ferry timing, and gutter recovery.
The gutter is continuous and the receiving ferry cycles vertically.

mechanics.fact: Isp alone can hold STEADY on the receiving ferry to stop its motor. The DELIVERY pad accepts either hero and light crates, requires total weight 2, and powers the signal bridge; a hero standing with the sac meets that threshold while the partner rides.

evidence.claim: The brake accepts Isp; DELIVERY accepts any occupant, requires two weights, and powers the bridge.
A light crate and hero each contribute one weight to an any-occupant pad.
An active power pad enables the required bridge; an active motor pad stops the ferry.

mechanics.fact: The mandatory exits are Pac's upper-right exit and Isp's lower-right exit. The source defines no collectibles and no hazard regions; a full-width gutter lies beneath the route.

evidence.claim: A continuous full-width gutter underlies the room.
No barriers or hazards/collectibles are authored, and the two exits are player-specific.

legal_routes.name: Accepted ordinary-input both-exits route: Pac takes upper exit, Isp takes lower exit

steps.goal: Set up the light sac and ferry/bridge sequence.
steps.action: The accepted replay crosses to the duct/ferry area and positions the sac for the low ferry transfer; Isp uses the unique STEADY pad when needed.
steps.expected_feedback: The ferry stops under Isp's hold; the sac can be pushed onto DELIVERY and paired with a hero to power the bridge.
steps.observed_feedback: The replay records 78 input intervals and completes the room with zero retries; this is prepared-route feasibility, not first-time discovery or human timing evidence.

evidence.claim: An ordinary-input sequence was replayed through both heroes' controls; empty-key segments do not establish required waiting.
Authored guidance confirms the intended sac/ferry/power sequence and gutter recovery.

steps.goal: Keep the bridge powered while Pac rides to the elevated exit.
steps.action: Isp and the sac occupy DELIVERY together; Pac rides the powered signal bridge to the upper finish and enters Pac's exit.
steps.expected_feedback: The powered bridge travels toward the upper-right finish; the lower floor remains available to Isp.
steps.observed_feedback: The replay ends with Pac at x=1063.19, y=94.00 and the room complete after Isp reaches the lower exit.

evidence.claim: The accepted replay completes with Pac at the upper exit and Isp at the lower exit, zero retries.
The signal bridge moves to the elevated upper finish when powered.

steps.goal: Reach Isp's matching exit along the continuous lower route.
steps.action: After Pac is safely through the high exit, Isp leaves the delivery position and walks along the gutter/floor to the lower-right exit.
steps.expected_feedback: Isp reaches the blue lower exit; both matching exits complete the level.
steps.observed_feedback: The accepted replay completes with Isp at x=1010.25, y=514.00 and Pac at x=1063.19, y=94.00.

evidence.claim: The route completes at the two distinct exit positions with no retries.
The exit coordinates are separated by height and player identity.
The accepted route set labels the position-46 path as a built-browser ordinary-input complete case.
The browser reported the level cleared in 0:53 with zero retries and 0/0 sparks.

steps.goal: Power the bridge with a hero and the sac, then use the bridge for the partner.
steps.action: Because DELIVERY accepts any hero or light crate and requires total weight 2, either hero can pair with the sac to power the bridge while the other rides; route the riders to their own exits.
steps.expected_feedback: The pad remains powered while the hero and sac occupy it; the other hero can ride the bridge.

evidence.claim: DELIVERY accepts any occupant and requires two weights.
A hero and light crate count as two pad weight.
Source supports either occupant pairing and distinct exits; this alternate was not separately replayed.

isp: Isp is the only hero accepted by STEADY, so Isp can brake the ferry for the low sac transfer.
Isp or Pac can stand with the sac on DELIVERY; the accepted route uses a hero-plus-sac weight to power the bridge.
Isp can then traverse the safe lower floor to the lower exit.
pac: Pac can bait Cana's nearest-target throw and help push the light sac through the duct/ferry route.
Pac can take the powered signal bridge to the upper exit while the partner keeps DELIVERY weighted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Letting Cana's boomerang target the nearest hero instead of using its path to nudge the sac.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp is briefly slowed or Pac is pushed; the projectile can also move the light sac, but a badly positioned hit can send it off the ferry.
common_mistakes.recovery: The effects expire quickly. The full-width gutter catches the sac; push it back toward the ferry and repeat the transfer. This recovery is source-authored guidance, not a separate replayed failure.

evidence.claim: Hint states nearest-hero targeting and gutter recovery.
Hit effects are temporary.

common_mistakes.mistake: Push the sac off the ferry when it is not low or miss the DELIVERY pad.
common_mistakes.consequence: The bridge does not receive the two-weight power supply and the high route remains unavailable.
common_mistakes.recovery: Recover the sac from the gutter and try the transfer on another ferry cycle; the receiving ferry repeats its six-second motion, and Isp can stop it with STEADY.

evidence.claim: Hint says to push the sac off while the ferry is low and recover it from the gutter if needed.
The ferry has a repeating six-second cycle.
Isp's hold pad stops the ferry; DELIVERY powers the bridge at two weight.

reasoning.rationale: The mandatory chain is now concrete: align Cana's nearest-target throw through the duct, deliver the light sac to a low ferry, use Isp's brake, pair the sac with a hero for two-weight power, and send the partner over the bridge. The first pass saw a vague recipient puzzle and missed the crate/weight chain; source and route evidence support several dependent decisions.

evidence.claim: Authored sequence names projectile alignment, sac transfer, ferry height, recovery, and bridge power.
The chain has distinct brake and weighted-power conditions.

cooperation.rationale: Isp alone can operate STEADY, and the powered bridge requires a hero-plus-sac weight while the partner rides; both must still reach different exits. The first pass recognized shared roles but missed the asymmetric brake and handoff.

evidence.claim: Isp-only brake and any-hero two-weight power pad create distinct contributions.
Both exits are reached by separate heroes.

execution.rationale: Both players must cross to the sac/ferry setup, push and reposition a light crate, manage a moving ferry, hold two weights, and traverse to vertically separated exits. The accepted replay confirms one complete route; it does not measure human precision. This replaces the first pass's undercount, which assumed mostly direct walking/jumping.

evidence.claim: The route uses a duct, ferry, powered bridge, and elevated finish.
A 78-interval prepared route reached both exits with zero retries.

timing.rationale: The sac must be pushed from a ferry when it is low, and the ferry follows a readable six-second repeating cycle that Isp can stop. The boomerang also has a visible windup; these create manageable timing/positioning decisions. This changes timing from unknown because the source proves a repeatable window, but does not establish a narrow window or human timing success.

evidence.claim: Receiving ferry repeats a six-second cycle.
Authored guidance directs the sac transfer while the ferry is low.

hazards.rationale: The authored level has no hazard regions and a continuous full-width gutter beneath the platforms. Boomerang dizzy/shove effects are temporary movement interference on safe floor, not mandatory physical danger. This resolves the first-pass unknown as absent/negligible on the mandatory route.

evidence.claim: A continuous floor/gutter spans the room bottom.
No barriers, hazards, or collectibles are authored.

novelty.rationale: Boomerang attacks were introduced at position 2, a two-weight powered lift at position 1, ferry braking at position 4, and a light pad-holding crate at position 8. This room recombines those taught ideas into projectile-guided sac delivery and a moving powered bridge; the initial score of 2 is supported, though it was not a wholly new brain/boomerang model.

evidence.claim: Boomerang attack first appears at campaign position 2.
Position 1 uses a two-weight powered lift.
Position 4 teaches an Isp-controlled ferry brake.
Position 8 adds a light movable box that can hold a pad.

recovery_cost.rationale: A misplaced sac falls to the full-width gutter and the authored hint explicitly says to recover it; the ferry repeats and can be stopped. That requires repeating some setup, but no lethal reset or long dependent sequence is indicated. The first pass could not estimate this recovery.

evidence.claim: Authored hint describes sac recovery from the gutter.
The gutter is continuous and ferry movement repeats.

solution_clarity.rationale: The visible subtitle and character dialogue point toward a wrong recipient and a sac stuck in a duct; the visible STEADY and DELIVERY 2 labels expose the key controls. The exact multi-step weight/bridge relation still requires testing. The first pass's score 3 overstated the cue burden because it ignored the source-confirmed role of the visible sac and pad labels; no hint was shown in the capture, so this remains a moderate burden.

evidence.claim: Visible subtitle/dialogue mention wrong recipient and a sac in a duct; the STEADY and DELIVERY 2 labels are visible.
The source-authored cue and hint confirm the intended connection without treating the hidden hint as visible.

control_friction.rationale: The accepted automated input route reaches completion, but it does not verify human shared-keyboard reliability, simultaneous two-person input, or interference under real hands. The first-pass null remains appropriate.

evidence.claim: A scripted accepted input schedule proves route feasibility but not human control friction.

confidence_reason: The source resolves the causal chain and the current campaign receipt replays a complete ordinary-input route with zero retries. Human discovery, control friction, subjective demand, and untried alternatives remain unmeasured.

confirmed: The high Pac exit and lower Isp exit are separate mandatory targets.
The throw interaction is central and both heroes must contribute before taking their exits.
missed_mechanics: Cana aims at the nearer hero but the boomerang also nudges the light sac; the intended task is to direct the projectile through the duct to reposition the sac.
Isp alone can stop the receiving ferry with STEADY.
A hero and the light sac together meet DELIVERY's two-weight threshold and power the bridge while the partner rides.
A misplaced sac is recoverable from the gutter; the ferry's low position is a repeatable window.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass treated the main relationship as selecting which hero receives the throw. The real intended interaction uses the projectile path on the sac; hitting a hero is temporary interference, not the route solution.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rose from 2 to 3 because the actual mandatory route contains several dependent causal steps involving projectile path, sac movement, ferry braking, two-weight power, and partner transport.
Cooperation rose from 2 to 3 because Isp has a unique brake role and one hero must sustain bridge power while the partner rides.
Execution rose from 2 to 3 because both heroes reposition the sac and traverse a moving ferry/powered bridge before using vertically separated exits.
Timing changed from unknown to 2 because the ferry repeats every six seconds and the authored route calls for pushing the sac while it is low; this does not prove a narrow or difficult human window.
Hazards changed from unknown to 0 after source inspection found no hazards and a continuous gutter. The temporary hero effects are interference on safe floor.
Recovery changed from unknown to 1 because the sac can be recovered from the gutter and the ferry can be retried; setup must be repeated but no lethal reset is authored.

Solution clarity decreased from burden 3 to 2: the screenshot already shows the duct/sac clue and STEADY/DELIVERY 2 labels, while the source confirms that these cues map to the route. The hint itself was closed and is not treated as visible.
unresolved: The accepted route demonstrates one ordinary-input path and zero retries, not first-time discovery or all legal routes.
An alternate hero-plus-sac assignment is supported by the any-occupant pad rule but was not separately replayed.
Human control friction and one-operator interference remain unknown.
No human success, enjoyment, frustration, or measured difficulty was observed.

single_operator_note: One operator must manage two movement schemes and watch the ferry/sac/bridge states; this adds simultaneous attention and key switching not included in the two-human scores, and its burden is not measured.
